D006-D010_h001.question:
It started around ten months ago. My wife says I “switched on.” I felt wired, like I didn’t need sleep, maybe three hours a night, and I was snapping at everyone over tiny things—students asking basic questions, my kids being a bit loud. At the same time, I was overflowing with ideas. I’d start three new papers in a night, volunteer for extra committees, redesign my whole syllabus, but I couldn’t finish anything. I’d jump from lecture slides to grant applications to reorganizing my office at 2 a.m., all half-done.

During this same stretch, for the past eight months, I’ve had this unnerving sense that the university is monitoring me. I’m convinced there are cameras in my office and that colleagues are trying to discredit me. Sometimes I feel things crawling on my skin, like ants on my arms or something touching my back, but there’s nothing there. I’ve even started using my own made-up shorthand words when I talk about it—my wife says I’m not making sense.

Then about three months ago, my energy crashed. I stopped returning emails, avoided colleagues, barely spoke at home. I’ve had a lot of “I’d be better off not waking up” thoughts, though I haven’t planned anything. During this low period, those paranoid ideas and the crawling sensations faded; they really only occur when I’m in that revved-up, irritable state.
D006-D010_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h001.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h002.question:

I’m ridiculously cheerful, even when we’ve just come back from a bad call, like nothing can touch me. Every little sound grabs me—the radio crackle, a car door outside, someone’s phone buzzing—and I’ll just lose my train of thought and jump to that.

Around 8 months ago, when this high really ramped up, I started seeing things. I’ll see men in turnout gear standing in corners or shadowy figures by the fire engine, but when I walk over, no one’s there. Sometimes at home I see people in our hallway, just staring. At the same time I became convinced people are watching me—my crew, the chief, even neighbors. I’ll check the windows, think there are cameras on the trucks or that dispatch is tracking my thoughts. When my mood briefly dipped for a few months and I felt empty, stopped surfing, and actually tried to overdose on my pain meds, those visions and beliefs disappeared; they only ever show up when I’m in that revved-up, “on top of the world” state.
D006-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

I’ve had moments standing on a balcony or at a busy street thinking, “If I just stepped off or into traffic, it would all stop.” I haven’t acted on it, but the urge scares me.     B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
